content.user_title: Build Go Collection Pipelines with samber/lo
content.value_statement: Manual Go collection transformations can become repetitive and difficult to optimize. This skill applies samber/lo helpers while explaining package choice, compatibility, errors, and performance tradeoffs.
actual_capabilities: Compares standard library functions with samber/lo helpers for common collection operations.
Refactors slice and map loops into typed Map, Filter, Reduce, GroupBy, and related transformations.
Selects among lo, lop, lom, loi, and experimental SIMD packages based on measured needs.
Applies error-aware variants such as MapErr and FilterErr to stop and propagate failures.
Explains mutation, concurrency, allocation, and Go version constraints for each package.
Provides reference guidance for slices, maps, strings, channels, tuples, math, and utility helpers.
limitations: It targets finite collection transformations, not reactive processing of infinite event streams.
Recommendations depend on the project Go version and the installed samber/lo release.
Performance advice does not replace application-specific profiles, benchmarks, or race testing.
Experimental SIMD APIs may change and require supported Go versions and amd64 systems.

use_cases.title: Refactor collection loops
use_cases.description: Convert repetitive slice and map loops into concise, typed samber/lo transformations while preserving behavior.

use_cases.title: Optimize data transformations
use_cases.description: Compare eager, parallel, mutable, and lazy approaches using workload size, CPU cost, allocation data, and Go version.

use_cases.title: Evaluate library adoption
use_cases.description: Assess where samber/lo adds value over standard library helpers and identify compatibility or maintenance tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a collection helper
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain whether samber/lo is appropriate for [operation] in a project targeting Go [version]. Compare the standard library and lo, then recommend one.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Go loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Go collection loop using samber/lo: [paste logic]. Preserve behavior, handle errors explicitly, and explain each selected helper.

prompt_templates.title: Select the right lo package
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this pipeline of [size] items and select lo, lop, lom, or loi. Consider CPU cost, allocations, mutation, concurrency, and Go version.

prompt_templates.title: Design a production pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production Go transformation for [input and goal] using samber/lo. Include error strategy, complexity, allocation tradeoffs, tests, and benchmark checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Choose between the standard library and samber/lo for checking membership in a string slice.
output: Recommendation: use slices.Contains when the project targets Go 1.21 or newer.
Reason: the standard library already covers direct membership checks without another helper.
Use lo.ContainsBy when membership requires a custom predicate.

output_examples.input: Select a package for three chained transformations over one million records on Go 1.23.
output: Recommendation: evaluate loi for a lazy, single-pass pipeline.
Benefit: lazy iteration can remove intermediate slice allocations.
Validation: compare memory profiles and benchmarks against the simpler lo implementation.

output_examples.input: Advise whether a request handler should use lo.Must when parsing user input.
output: Recommendation: return and handle the parsing error explicitly.
Risk: lo.Must converts invalid input into a panic.
Reserve lo.Must for startup or test failures where termination is intentional.

best_practices: Provide the Go version, data size, workload type, and current implementation with each request.
State whether mutation, output order, partial failures, and cancellation are acceptable.
Profile and benchmark before adopting mutable, parallel, lazy, or experimental variants.
anti_patterns: Do not request parallel helpers without describing whether work is CPU-bound or input sizes are large.
Do not replace standard library helpers solely because samber/lo is already installed.
Do not use panic-based helpers for routine failures in handlers or long-running services.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It selects and applies samber/lo helpers for typed transformations across Go collections and related utility types.

faq.question: Which Go versions are supported?
faq.answer: Core, parallel, and mutable packages require Go 1.18 or newer. Lazy iterators require Go 1.23 or newer.

faq.question: Should I always prefer samber/lo over the standard library?
faq.answer: No. Prefer standard library helpers when they directly cover the operation and use lo for missing transformations.

faq.question: When should I use lop?
faq.answer: Use lop for expensive CPU-bound transformations when benchmarks show that parallel execution offsets goroutine overhead.

faq.question: Does lo modify input collections?
faq.answer: Core lo functions return new collections. The lom package performs explicit in-place mutation and requires careful ownership.

faq.question: Can this skill optimize streaming pipelines?
faq.answer: No. It targets finite collections. Reactive or infinite event streams require a streaming library such as samber/ro.
